session.question: In the study, how did PC affect EE, and what was the impact of EE and SI on SS?
session.answer:
Perceived curiosity (PC) had a significant positive effect on effort expectancy (EE), indicating that higher curiosity was associated with greater expected ease of use of the Metaverse. However, neither EE nor social influence (SI) had a significant impact on social sustainability (SS); both relationships were statistically non-significant in the model. (alkhwaldi2024investigatingthesocial chunk 1)

Thus, PC increased EE, but EE did not translate into a meaningful effect on SS, and SI also did not significantly predict SS. (alkhwaldi2024investigatingthesocial chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-76670276: The study added perceived curiosity (PC) and extraversion (EXT) to a UTAUT-based model to examine students’ perceptions of the Metaverse’s social sustainability (SS) in Jordanian universities. Structural equation modeling with 422 students showed that PC significantly affected effort expectancy (EE). However, EE and social influence (SI) did not have a significant impact on SS. In contrast, performance expectancy (PE), facilitating conditions (FC), and extraversion (EXT) significantly influenced SS.
From Abeer F. Alkhwaldi. Investigating the social sustainability of immersive virtual technologies in higher educational institutions: students’ perceptions toward metaverse technology. Sustainability, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su16020934, doi:10.3390/su16020934.

pqac-79a7e3bb: The study examined how perceived curiosity (PC), effort expectancy (EE), social influence (SI), and social sustainability (SS) relate in students’ perceptions of Metaverse technology in Jordanian higher education. Structural equation modeling showed that PC significantly and positively affected EE. However, EE and SI were found to have no significant impact on SS. Thus, PC influences SS only indirectly through EE, but EE does not translate into a significant effect on SS, and SI also does not significantly predict SS.
From Abeer F. Alkhwaldi. Investigating the social sustainability of immersive virtual technologies in higher educational institutions: students’ perceptions toward metaverse technology. Sustainability, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su16020934, doi:10.3390/su16020934.

pqac-994e6302: The excerpt describes a study on creative accounting practices (CAP) and its antecedents and effects in Bangladeshi listed firms. It reports that political connections (PC), corporate ethical values (CEV), future company orientations (FCO), and corporate governance practices (CGP) are antecedents of CAP, while sustainable financial data (SFD) is not. CAP positively affects quality of financial reporting (QFR) and negatively affects decision-making effectiveness (DME); QFR then positively affects DME. The excerpt does not mention EE, SI, or SS, so no relationships among those variables are provided here.
From Muhammad Shajib Rahman, Md Jahid Hasan, Md Saddam Hossain Khan, and Ishrat Jahan. Antecedents and effect of creative accounting practices on organizational outcomes: evidence from bangladesh. Heliyon, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heliyon.2023.e13759, doi:10.1016/j.heliyon.2023.e13759.
